picked.title: QVS-LIVO RiskMap: Health- and Information-Aware View Selection for Multi-Camera LIVO and Off-Road Risk Mapping
picked.summary: Multi-camera observations in off-road environments vary significantly in reliability, posing challenges when complementing degraded geometric constraints. Motivated by this, we propose Quality-aware View Selection Lidar-Vision Odometry Risk Mapping (QVS-LIVO RiskMap), which decouples visual processing for state estimation from that for semantic mapping. The front end evaluates camera observations through read-only pretracking on a shared lidar-inertial posterior, combining observation health with geometric complementarity. Channel health memory and switching hysteresis govern selection of at most one eligible view for direct photometric correction. The posterior is retained when no view is eligible or the correction fails acceptance. The mapping back end integrates semantic observations from all available views in a shared world grid. Vehicle-scale geometry constrains semantic risk corrections, while spatial and temporal evidence supports risk confirmation. The system also produces a local bird's-eye-view (BEV) risk map and a global 2.5D semantic-terrain risk map with obstacle instance voxels. On two field sequences, QVS-LIVO achieved horizontal root mean square errors of 0.910 m and 1.664 m. It reduced error by 43.3% relative to FAST-LIO2 on the degraded long-route sequence. Across 12 controlled camera-fault configurations involving dropout, black frames and 60 ms timestamp shifts, it maintained complete trajectories with errors of 1.54-2.23 m. When deployed onboard an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, the system generates local and global maps at 9.94 Hz and 2.00 Hz, respectively, with a median local mapping latency of 32.4 ms. These runtime results demonstrate the real-time feasibility of selective visual state updates alongside multi-view semantic mapping under challenging off-road conditions. The code and related resources are available at: https://github.com/zihanPan-HIT/QVS-LIVO.

picked.title: Genie Sim Benchmark: Real-to-Sim Fidelity and Evaluation
picked.summary: We evaluate Genie Sim Benchmark through paired real-simulation tasks and complementary system-identification studies. Across 22 robot-task pairs spanning 16 task names, task-specific pi0.5 policies fine-tuned on real-robot data achieve a descriptive Score correlation of 0.9686, MAE 0.0405, RMSE 0.0520, with simulation-real differences from -0.110 to +0.080. G2 crsB experiments assess long-horizon closed-loop position and joint-side torque agreement, while five representative object cases examine identification and cross-engine contact transfer. A separate 32.6503 s teleoperation trajectory, excluded from mechanical identification and servo-gain search, evaluates external position targets through simulated motion-controller command shaping and a calibrated position servo. Across both arms, per-joint position RMSE spans 0.00614-0.03522 rad and current-derived torque RMSE spans 0.73545-4.00099 N m. Native PhysX adaptations recover three recorded interaction tasks, with case-dependent alignment gains. These results support task-specific simulation evaluation through joint assessment of task outcomes and physical-response consistency.

picked.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
picked.summary: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.

picked.summary: 西湖世界模型研究中心成立，施一公亲自揭牌。世界模型赛道已经不缺创业公司。 海外李飞飞、Yann LeCun 等学术大佬亲自下场，国内极佳视界、逆矩阵、流形空间等创业公司高密度入场。 但最近几个月，入场的力量开始发生变化，下场的不再只是公司，高校和地方政府也开始组织力量，参与这场技术竞争。 今年 7 月，北京大学与逆矩阵科技成立世界模型联合实验室。10 月，由极佳视界牵头的通用世界模型北京市重点实验室揭牌。一个是高校与创业公司联合研发，一个是北京市支持建设的重点科研平台。 如今，西湖大学再落一子，成立世界模型研究中心。西湖大学校长、中国科学院院士施一公亲自揭牌。 与研究中心同时亮相的，还有首版基础模型 Awomo-0.5。这款仅有 40 亿参数的模型，在6项国际公开评测的不同榜单中同时登顶，涉及物理推理、机器人操作和泛化等任务。 更值得关注的是，西湖大学 团队 已经开展了三年世界模型研究，建有自主智能实验室 AutoLab。 有实验室，还有阶段性技术成果， 为什么还要成立一个校级研究中心？先看它想把世界模型做到什么程度。 01 40亿参数“概念世界模型”， 瞄准通用物理智能 西湖大学 团队 发布的首版基础模型 Awomo-0.5，定位是 通用物理世界模型 。它希望让 AI 学习能够跨场景复用的物理规律，理解物体之间的关系，并预测真实世界接下来会发生什么。 这款模型只有 4B（40 亿）参数，采用的是 “概念世界模型”（Concept World Model） 技术路线。 …

picked.title: Video Friday: NASA PROMISEs a New Moon Rover
picked.summary: NASA will send a nuclear-powered rover called PROMISE (Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration, depicted in the rendering) to the Moon’s South Pole as a foundational mission in the Moon Base Program. It will be constructed largely from existing hardware—test-bed and flight-spare components—developed for NASA’s ongoing Mars rover missions, Curiosity and Perseverance. [ NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory ] What happens when you put wheels on a humanoid and let a learned controller drive it? We swapped the feet on our Atlas robot to find out; it let us push our actuators, and our models of them, hard. [ Boston Dynamics ] The Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials and Mass-efficient Design (NOM4D) program has achieved the first ever demonstration of automated in-space assembly. A California Institute of Technology (Caltech) payload operating in orbit built a truss structure from individual components. A relatively simple gantry robot (able to move along three linear axes) connected composite truss members using custom-designed joints while simultaneously deploying a thin reflective mesh; a proof-of-concept for future space-based antennas.
